name: My Introduction to Engineering (MITE)
org: Cockrell School of Engineering, The University of Texas at Austin
what_you_do: This is a five-day residential summer camp for rising seniors. You live on campus. Your team does an engineering project and hands-on activities. You spend time with engineering students, faculty and alumni.
who_can_apply: Current high school juniors with a strong interest in engineering, science or math who live in the United States. About 56 students per session are chosen by holistic review. Students from low-income backgrounds or with limited STEM access are strongly encouraged to apply.
pay_detail: $500, paid only after acceptance (students stay in a campus residence hall)
duration: 5 days (June 13 to 17 and July 25 to 29 in 2027)
deadline_text: Applications open in December 2026 (no day is given) and close Feb 28, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. Central. No late applications.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the MITE page. Questions: cseoutreach@utexas.edu.
notes: Selective. The page does not list a financial-aid policy; ask cseoutreach@utexas.edu if the $500 is a barrier.
